The government of Mexico will request today the support of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), so that in coordination with the competent authorities of Honduras, Guatemala and El Salvador, and in conjunction with the National Institute of Migration (INM) and the Mexican Commission for Assistance to Refugees (Comar), accompany the attention of possible refugee applicants who may appear on the southern border of Mexico.

The request for UNHCR support will be formally presented today by the Secretary of Foreign Affairs of Mexico, Luis Videgaray Caso, during the meeting he will hold with the Secretary General of the United Nations (UN), Antonio Guterres, in New York .

"This measure is intended to contribute to a humanitarian solution, attached to the legal framework, respectful of human rights, transparent and with the help of the international community, through the corresponding bodies of the United Nations Organization.

Likewise, this measure seeks to guarantee the safety and integrity of migrants, particularly that of minors, the elderly and women, and to prevent people from being deceived by international criminal organizations dedicated to the trafficking of persons, which endanger them. their lives, "says the SRE in a statement.

The Mexican government reiterated:

  1. That any person wishing to enter national territory must do so in compliance with the requirements established in the Migration Law and through authorized entry points, and may move freely in it for the duration of the visa.

  2. That the current legislation does not provide for a document granting admission to Mexico without meeting requirements to transit to a neighboring country.

  3. That any person who enters the national territory and wishes to request the recognition of refugee status or be a beneficiary of complementary protection measures, must do so individually, in accordance with current legislation and international law.

Finally, the Mexican government said that it reiterates its commitment to the efforts of the international community in favor of safe, orderly and regular migration; and with the human rights of migrants. At the same time, it expresses its conviction that international dialogue and cooperation between the countries of origin, transit and destination of migrants are indispensable to face the challenges implied by the migratory phenomenon.

How can I preserve food without a refrigerator and freezer? Is there a way dry ice can help with that? Like are there other methods for preserving food that would normally be stored in a freezer. Thanks everyone.
How can I preserve food without a refrigerator and freezer?

Dehydration, fermentation, or canning.

For dehydration, you can dehydrate fruit with a bit of sulphur as a preservative, and meats with salt as a preservative.

Fermentation of veggies usually involves a salt brine to help encourage the proper bacteria to grow, those bacteria, lactobacillus in particular, produce lactic acid, which further inhibits the growth of unwelcome bacteria.

For canning, everything gets sterilized as part of the process, so there's nothing alive to spoil the food.
Canning or dehydration, depending on what you're trying to preserve. Root cellars work for veggetables.
Salting, smoking, pickling, drying are all methods of food preservation that don't require electricity. Dry ice won't last, btw.
In addition to what has been mentioned some things can be vacuum sealed.

This is more for freezing to protect against "freezer burn". Vacuum sealing does nothing to stop the growth of bacteria. You have to have fully sterilized food before it gets sealed. Same with canning food. That is why the food is taken to a very high temp inside a sterile container before sealing. Hot things and plastic don't go together so really, this is not a preservation-without-refrigeration strategy.
I once read how effective the inside of a waterfall would be for keeping milk from spoiling by some delightful children residing in an abandoned boxcar.

Anything specifically you're looking to preserve?

Veggies and fruits can be canned/fermented. Meat can be cured/salted (prepare for the rabbit hole of charcuterie). Aside from that certain veggies like potatoes, turnips, carrots, etc can be cellared or simply buried under ground again.
Sand. Root vegetables can be layered in sand.
Move to a very cold place and put it outside.

Sourdough lasts by defending itself with its own yeast and low pH.

Ferments like (unpasteurized) beer, sauerkraut, kim chi, pickled things all stay good for a long time.

Dried/smoked/salted folds lasts a long time.

As for "what do I do with my frozen food when the power goes out", get a generator. Frozen food isn't designed to last when not frozen.

Before or after SHTF?

If before: canned food, freeze drying, dehydration, curing, salting, pemmican-style, high amounts of sugar (such as storing in honey)

After: smoking, dehydration, salting, limited curing (be careful, botulism is a bitch), salting, pemmican-style, honey-based sugar preserving.
